full_judgment:
2. The petitioners as plaintiffs instituted the title suit for declaration of title and recovery of Khas possession imp leading the opposite parties as defendants. 

 12. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 31-10-2001, the plaintiffs as appellants preferred Title Appeal No. 206 of 2001 before the learned District Judge, Comilla. On transfer the appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Comilla, who dismissed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree of the Joint District Judge taking the same view as was taken by the learned trial Court to the effect that the plaintiffs have failed to prove their possession on the basis of two title deeds and that as the plaintiffs have failed to prove their possession in the suit land, so they cannot get decree of recovery of khas possession. 

 46. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 23-3-2004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Comilla dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 31-10-2001 passed by the Joint District Judge, First Court, Comilla are set aside. The suit is decreed and the Plaintiffs do get khas possession of the suit land.
